The direct-cooling cooling tower is located near the WGS quench tower to optimize the power requirement for the pump. The main component of the direct cooling water (DCW) system is a mechanical induced-draft cooling tower counter flow type with FRP construction and with PVC fills with basin, DCW circulation pumps, chemical injection facilities, and DCW Distribution and Collection Headers. Circulation water is cooled in the 3-cell cooling tower from a bulk return temperature of 158°F down to 90°F based on 75°F wet bulb temperature. The cooling tower basin and pump forebay provide 15 minutes of storage of the total circulating rate of 9,840 GPM water. The DM water requirement for this project is estimated to be approx. 925 GPM. The treatment unit has three (3) streams (2 workings + 1 standby) for ease of operation and maintenance. 7.2.1 Design Basis The broad technology for the treatment is an RO system followed by a conventional mixed bed DM plant. The capacity of each stream in the RO-DM plant (as well as individual equipment) is designed to produce the required output quantity and includes the additional requirement of DM water for regeneration purposes/backwash of exchangers.
